postings.description:
Description of the Agency's tasks

ECHA is the driving force among regulatory authorities in implementing the EU's ground-breaking chemicals legislation for the benefit of human health and the environment as well as for innovation and competitiveness. ECHA helps companies to comply with the legislation, promotes the safe use of chemicals, provides information on chemicals and addresses chemicals of concern. You will find more information on ECHA and the different Regulations on ECHA website at: http://www.echa.europa.eu

General requirements

Candidates for secondment must:

• Have current employment in the national, regional or local public sector or international civil service. Alternatively candidates may be employed in a non-profit or voluntary sector;

• Hold a university degree in a field relevant to the areas of work described in this call;

• Be a national of an EU or EFTA Member State or a candidate country as decided by the Council;

• Be able to communicate in written and spoken English as this is the working language of ECHA.

Secondment

The secondment will be subject to an exchange of letters between the Head of People and Development of ECHA and the applicant’s employer. The duration of the first secondment is a maximum of one year. This period may be renewed for a maximum of three additional years.

Seconded National Experts remain in the service of their employer throughout the period of their secondment. The sending organisation must continue remunerating the SNE, who will thus benefit from social security coverage. During their secondment, SNEs will receive subsistence allowances and reimbursement of expenses as set out in the “Rules on the secondment of national experts to the European Chemicals Agency” (Decision ED-0050).

The SNE Rules

Profile

Seconded National Expert – Communications Officer; ref.: ECHA/SNE/2026/002

Our ideal candidate is a communications professional with experience gained working in a national authority, national ministry, European institution or European agency. Comfortable in a changing environment, you are adaptable, resilient and have good interpersonal and networking skills. You are curious about developments in your field and communications more broadly.

The Unit is responsible for ECHA’s communications activities, including press relations, external and internal communications, social media, digital communications and its website. We focus on delivering professional proactive, clear and strategic communications services, that support the Agency’s activities and promote ECHA’s work and achievements.

We support the delivery of ECHA’s mandate, purpose, vision and goals through:

• building, maintaining and protecting ECHA’s reputation by enhancing its visibility and stakeholder engagement;

• promoting chemical safety through science, collaboration and knowledge;

• positioning ECHA as the EU’s chemicals agency;

• ensuring that relevant, reliable and objective information is available for the public and interested parties; and

• optimising communications channels for effective outreach.

Job description:

The Seconded National Expert will work in the Communications Unit – G3.

The Communications Officer will contribute to the Unit’s daily interaction with internal and external stakeholders. The jobholder will also be responsible for relations with internal business areas on specific regulatory topics in support of ECHA’s external communications strategy. The role for this profile will be assigned according to the Unit’s needs and the jobholders’ competencies.

Duties will include, depending on needs:

External Communications:

• Drafting press releases, briefings, speeches etc.;

• Developing content for ECHA’s website;

• Dealing with press queries, interviews and briefings;

• Supporting senior management with media appearances;

• Organising and supporting events for external stakeholders;

• Support the production of webinars and videos;

• Support the management of the Agency's corporate communication channels and social media presence;

• Acting as a spokesperson when required; and

• Working with colleagues across ECHA to determine communication priorities and key messages to be delivered to internal and external stakeholders.

Internal Communications:

• Cooperating with colleagues in determining communications priorities;

• Content development for ECHA’s Intranet;

• Organising and supporting internal staff events; and

• General support to internal communication initiatives.

The Unit is responsible for a number of ECHA wide projects, where input may be required, including:

• Building a new website;

• Implementing the new ECHA corporate identity;

• ECHA’s 2027 Conference – 20-21 May 2027;

• ECHA’s 20th Anniversary 1 June 2027-31 May 2028;

• Chairing the EU Agencies Heads of Communications & Information Network – 1 March 2027 28 February 2028;

Requirements:

Successful completion of a full course of university studies attested by a degree, where the normal duration of university education is three (3) years or more.

Of your total professional experience, at least one (1) year must be in a field or fields relevant to the areas of work mentioned above e.g. for example, external/internal communications or stakeholder relations.

Only qualifications issued by EU Member State authorities or EEA authorities and qualifications recognised as equivalent by the relevant EU or EEA Member State authorities will be accepted.

Selection criteria: If you meet the requirements set out above, you will be assessed on the basis of the following selection criteria.

The candidates who are judged to be the most suitable on the basis of the selection criteria will be invited to a (remote) interview. The following will be considered as assets:

• Ability to communicate effectively in English at all levels both orally and in writing;

• Experience of working in a communications/stakeholder relations function in a complex regulatory environment; and

• Demonstrated understanding of the link between your current experience, the Communications Officer’s role and ECHA’s strategic priorities.

How to apply?

In order to be considered, applications must:

• Be submitted online, through the Apply button

• Include the following mandatory documents:

- CV in European Format: saved with CV_selection title_your surname and first name http://echa.europa.eu/documents/10162/17100/europass_cv_en.doc

- Employer Statement: saved with Employer statement_selection title_your surname and first name http://echa.europa.eu/documents/10162/17100/sne_employer_statement_en.pdf

- Letter of Motivation: saved with Motivation letter_selection title_your surname and first name

Candidates are requested to submit one application per profile. Candidates applying for several profiles should submit a separate application for each profile. Applications for each profile will be considered and assessed separately.

After successfully submitting your application, a confirmation message will appear on your screen and you will receive an automatically generated email as an acknowledgement of receipt, sent to the email address that you provided in the form.

Please contact us at traineeshipsecha [dot] europa [dot] eu (traineeships[at]echa[dot]europa[dot]eu) if you are not able to successfully submit your application.

NB: Applications that are incomplete or do not fulfil the criteria set out above will not be taken into account.

Assessment of application

Applicants will be assessed on the basis of their academic and professional qualifications and their relevance to the job. Short-listed candidates will be required to undergo a telephone and/or face-to-face interview. Human Resources will contact the successful candidates and their employers to initiate an exchange of letters between the Agency and the employers.

Protection of personal data

The information submitted during the selection process will be used solely for that purpose. Organisational setting:
The post of Specialist – Data Storage & Infrastructure Operations is located in the Infrastructure Services Team, ICT Operations Unit, ICT Department, Capabilities Directorate.

The C1 ICT Department has the responsibility for devising, delivering and operating critical technology capabilities and solutions supporting the core mission and support processes of Europol. Over 150 internal staff members and a significant number of domain-specific consultants are responsible for devising, developing, delivering and operating information management and communication technology capabilities that ensure enhanced criminal information analysis and exchange among Europol, Member States and third parties.

The ICT Operations Unit is responsible for the operations and management of the Europol ICT Infrastructure. This includes Workplace services, Service Management, Network Services, Platform Services, Application Services, Infrastructure Services and ICT Security.

Purpose of the post:
The role of the Specialist – Data Storage & Infrastructure Operations is in charge of installing, maintaining and supporting of ICT Infrastructure with particular focus on Server-based computing technologies, including data backup/restore, enterprise email services and archiving solutions.

Further tasks include the implementation of the infrastructure solutions in line with design and the provision of 2nd/3rd level support for the solutions in scope.

Reporting lines:
The incumbent reports to the Senior Specialist - Head of Team – Infrastructure Services / Head of Unit – ICT Operations.

This post will require participation in a shift system including weekends and nights as well as on-call duty.

- Actively review Architecture and Engineering guidelines to ensure manageability and full understanding of technical consequences;
- Review and implement technical requirements for ICT infrastructure solutions including relevant security controls;
- Develop and maintain sufficient knowledge about the interdependencies of all infrastructure components deployed in the production environment in order to prevent incidents and problems;
- Acting as a second and third level support, perform technical analysis, investigation, troubleshooting and resolution of incidents or problems affecting the Europol ICT infrastructure;
- Provide support to capacity management activities, recommending changes in ICT infrastructure in order to address capacity demands;

- Monitor technology developments maintaining up-to-date knowledge of state-of-the-art solutions;
- Perform any other tasks in the area of competence as assigned by the line management.

- Be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen;
- Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service;
- Produce appropriate character references as to his or her suitability for the performance of the duties;
- Be physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post as further specified in Article 13 of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS);
- Produce evidence of a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the Union to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties.

b. Candidates must have

- A level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma;

OR

- Professional training of an equivalent level in a relevant area and after having completed the training, at least the number of years of relevant professional experience as indicated below:

Duration of professional training Additional professional experience required for equivalency

- Experience with data Backup/Restore and Disaster Recovery;
- Experience with server and application virtualization implementation and support, such as VMware technologies;
- Hands-on experience, preferably five years or more, with installation and maintenance of Microsoft Exchange Server on-premises (2016/2019);

Desirable:

- Experience with Server-based computing technologies (e.g. Citrix, XenApp or others);

b. Professional knowledge

- Knowledge of recent Microsoft (and/or RedHat) Server Operating systems and their security and maintenance aspects;
- Knowledge of Microsoft Exchange Server on-premises (2016/2019) and integration with Microsoft Active Directory;
- Knowledge of Active Directory Domain Services and integrated systems on large and complex environments;
- Knowledge of server and application virtualization with VMware configuration and related troubleshooting;

Communicating:

- Produce evidence of a thorough knowledge of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge of another language of the Union to the extent necessary for the performance of the duties.

b. Candidates must have

Duration of professional training Additional professional experience required for equivalency

4. Requirements - Selection criteria

Selection criteria:
a. Professional experience:
Essential

- Preferably at least 5 years’ experience in digital forensics using standard forensic tools (commercial and open-source solutions);
- Experience in automating the processing and indexing of large structured and unstructured datasets;
- Experience in designing, building, and operating automated processing pipelines or workflow orchestration;
- Experience in software development in Python with proficiency in PowerShell, Bash and command-line scripting;
- Experience working with SQL and structured data stores, including SQLite;
- Experience with containerisation (Docker) and CI/CD, and with developing reusable APIs, libraries, plugins or automation frameworks.

Desirable:

- Experience integrating multiple third-party tools and services into end-to-end automated workflows via REST APIs, command-line interfaces and JSON/XML;
- Experience applying AI technologies to support digital forensic workflows;
- Experience integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into automation solutions.

b. Professional knowledge:
Essential:

- Knowledge in digital forensics investigation and examination techniques, including acquisition methods, file systems, data minimisation and chain of custody;
- Knowledge in Windows and Linux operating systems and their forensic artefacts;
- Knowledge of software engineering principles, including testing, debugging, and version control;
- Ability to analyse existing forensic processes, identify opportunities for automation, and engineer scalable, maintainable, and validated workflow solutions;
- Knowledge of Indexing and search at scale: text extraction, OCR, deduplication, index integrity, and the behaviour of Lucene/Elasticsearch/dtSearch-style engines.

Desirable:

- Applying AI and LLM’s within automation solutions, including their limitations, explainability and validation requirements in an evidential context.

c. General competencies
Essential:
Communicating:

- Very good communication skills in English, both orally and in writing;
- Ability to draft clear and concise documents on complex matters for various audiences.

Analysing & problem solving:

- Keen eye for detail with the ability to maintain standards of accuracy under pressure of tight deadlines;
- Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills;
- Competent user of Microsoft Office applications (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) and the internet.

Delivering quality and results:

- High degree of commitment and flexibility;
- High level of customer and service-orientation.

Prioritising and organising:

- Good administrative and organisational skills;
- Very good interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well, both independently and in a team;

Resilience:

- Ability to remain effective under a heavy workload and demonstrate resistance to stress;
- Ability to handle exposure to disturbing child sexual abuse content while maintaining professional judgement and personal wellbeing.

Living diversity:

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multi-cultural environment.

d. Additional conditions:
Fulfil the condition stipulated in Article 5 of the Decision of the Executive Director on the Duration of contracts of employment for Temporary Agents, on the start date of the possible contract of employment which may be offered.

5. Selection procedure

All applications for Temporary Agent posts must be submitted through the online recruitment system accessible via Europol’s website. For further information, please consult the Europol Recruitment Guidelines.

The Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (AACC) sets up a Selection Committee, composed of at least three members, consisting of one chair and at least one member from the administration and one member designated by the Staff Committee.

For restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), the AACC designates up to two additional members of the Selection Committee if so requested by the Chairperson of the Management Board. The additional members shall consist of a representative of the Presidency of the Council of the European Union or one representative of the Presidency and one representative of another Member State.

The selection criteria, set out in this Vacancy Notice, will be assessed by the Selection Committee throughout the different stages of the selection procedure. Before the start of the selection procedure, the Selection Committee will decide which selection criteria will be used at each stage of the selection procedure. Certain selection criteria will be assessed only for shortlisted candidates during a written test and/or a competency-based interview.

The Selection Committee will assess the applications received in order to make an initial selection of those candidates meeting all eligibility criteria and matching best the selection criteria (suitability).

In case of candidates shortlisted for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts), who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, Europol will seek confirmation from the relevant Europol National Unit to ensure that those candidates indeed belong to a competent authority.

The minimum pass-mark for being shortlisted, i.e. invited to participate in a post-related selection procedure, consisting of a written test and a competency-based interview, is established as 60% of the total maximum score.

The Selection Committee will shortlist the 8 highest scoring candidates. All candidates having a score equal to the 8th highest scoring candidate will be invited to take part in the selection procedure. At shortlisting stage, the Selection Committee will establish the pass-mark for the selection procedure.

It is intended for the selection procedure to be conducted remotely. Should the Selection Committee consider it necessary to conduct the selection procedure on-site at Europol, either in part or in full, in the interest of the proceedings, and subject to budget availability, the candidates invited to participate in the selection procedure will be informed accordingly.

After the selection procedure has taken place, the Selection Committee will establish a list of successful candidates, i.e. those scoring above the pre-defined pass-mark, which is shared with the AACC, for establishment of a Reserve list. A Reserve list is valid for 24 months.

Candidates who participated in the interview will be informed of the outcome, i.e. whether they have been successful or not.

6. Compensation and benefits

Scale: AD6
The gross basic monthly salary is EUR 6,961.29 (step 1) or EUR 7,253.84 (step 2).

The step in grade is determined on the basis of professional experience gained after the education required for the post and in line with applicable implementing rules.

Staff pay EU tax at source but salaries are exempt from national taxes. Compulsory deductions are made for health insurance, pension and unemployment insurance.

Subject to the applicable conditions being met, as defined in the EU Staff Regulations (EUSR)/CEOS and further specified in the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union, allowances such as expatriation allowance (16% of basic gross salary) or foreign residence allowance (4% of basic gross salary), household allowance, dependent child and / or education allowance may be granted.

Staff enjoy worldwide insurance coverage by the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS) and are insured against sickness, the risk of occupational disease and accident.

Europol offers flexible working arrangements, a comprehensive provision for annual leave as well as parental leave supporting a healthy work-life balance.

7. Terms and conditions

Contract of employment
The successful candidate will be engaged in the type of post Administrator and function group AD, grade 6 pursuant to Article 2(f) CEOS and Annex I to the EUSR.
The initial contract will be concluded for a period of 5 years (full-time – 40 hours a week). The contract may be renewed only once, in principle, for a period of 5 years.
The overall duration of the contracts on restricted posts of Europol staff members will be taken into account if they are successful in the selection procedure.

Conditions of engagement
Before the employment contract is concluded by Europol, the successful candidate will have to:

- declare any conflict of interest;
- undergo a pre-employment medical examination to confirm that he/she is physically fit to perform the duties pertaining to the post or, alternatively, receive the confirmation from Europol that he/she fulfils the conditions laid down in the Decision of the Deputy Executive Director of the Capabilities Directorate on the pre-employment medical examination available on www.europol.europa.eu;
- in case of candidates for restricted posts (including restricted - Annex II posts) who had indicated membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States, provide confirmation of his/her membership of a competent authority in one of the Member States within the meaning of the Article 2(a) of the Europol Regulation.
The place of employment will be The Hague, The Netherlands.
For further information on terms and conditions, please consult the EUSR/CEOS available on Europol’s website www.europol.europa.eu

Probation period
Engagement for this post is subject to the successful completion of a probationary period of 9 months.

Europol reserves the right to terminate the contract of employment during or at the end of the probation period in accordance with Article 14 CEOS.

Security screening and certificate of good conduct
Candidates who have been recruited to a post at Europol are required to furnish a valid certificate of good conduct before the start of their employment. The certificate of good conduct must be provided to Europol prior to the signature of the employment contract. The certificate of good conduct must be issued by the relevant authorities of the country of nationality of the candidate and must not be older than three months at the time of submission to Europol. Europol reserves the right not to proceed with the signature of the contract based on the content of the certificate or if the candidate fails to provide the certificate to Europol.

The certificate of good conduct does not substitute a valid security clearance required for all Europol staff at the level indicated in the vacancy notice. Failure to obtain the requisite security clearance may be cause for termination of the employment contract.

Candidates who currently hold a valid security clearance at the level indicated in the vacancy notice or above do not need to obtain a certificate of good conduct or a new security clearance and must provide a copy of the current security clearance certificate to Europol prior to the signature of the employment contract. Europol shall verify and confirm the continued validity of the security clearance. In case Europol determines that the security clearance is not valid, the candidate will be required to provide a valid certificate of good conduct prior to the signature of the employment contract. Europol may at any time terminate the employment contract if the result of the security screening is not positive and the necessary clearance level is not granted or extended.

VACANCY NOTICE FOR
  TEMPORARY AGENT SELECTION
Job title  Translator/Language Technology Coordinator
Reference  DGT/COM/2026/1916
Application deadline  16.10.2026 - 12.00 (Brussels time)
Directorate-General (full name)  Directorate-General for Translation
Unit  Swedish-language unit 2 (DGT.B.1.SV.2)
Place of assignment  Luxembourg
Grade range  AD5 - AD7
Domain  Languages, Information Technology
Contract type  Temporary Agent 2b

About us (“We are”)

We are DGT.B.1.SV.2, based in Luxembourg, one of the two units of the Swedish
language community at the Directorate General for Translation (DGT). Our mission
is to provide the Commission with high-quality translations into Swedish from all EU
languages, but mainly from English. We translate texts for different requester DGs
and services, in a wide variety of subject areas such as agriculture, regional policy,
health and food safety, internal market and industry, education and culture,
employment and social affairs.

About the role (“We propose”)

We offer a challenging and stimulating job as a translator and language technology
coordinator in a stable and well-integrated unit with some 25 translators and
assistants. The documents to be translated are mainly of a legal, administrative,
political or technical nature. However, we also translate press material, web texts
and documents intended for the general public. As a translator, you have the
opportunity to acquire new skills in a rich linguistic environment and use advanced
IT tools supporting the translation process. In addition to translating, you will revise
texts translated by colleagues and evaluate outsourced translations. You may also
specialise in a specific subject domain, develop working methods, be involved in
quality assurance and terminology work or act as lead translator for specific
translation projects. As a language technology coordinator, you will help promote
and raise awareness of available language technology, translation tools and

applications, and AI tools applied to translation. Furthermore, you will contribute to
testing and deployment of translation tools and applications in DGT and provide first
level technical support and advice regarding the use of these tools and applications.
The job involves close cooperation with all colleagues in the unit as well as with
Brussels-based colleagues, DGT's Language Technology community and DGT's
Field Officers in Stockholm and Helsinki.

Qualifications, experience and skills (“We look for”)

We look for a dynamic, team-oriented and reliable colleague with an excellent
command of Swedish (mother tongue), very good knowledge of English and
knowledge of at least one other official language of the European Union. Very good
general IT skills and practical experience with IT applications are indispensable, as
well as very good knowledge of language technology and translation tools and
applications. An interest and willingness to develop further in this area is also
essential since our working environment is highly technical. Studies and/or
experience in the fields of finance, economics, science or law are an asset, as is
knowledge or experience in the requesting DGs’ subject areas. Since we are a small
team, versatility and an ability to cover a broad range of the unit's portfolios and text
types are seen as an advantage. The job requires very good communication skills
and an ability to work closely with colleagues in a team of translators and assistants,
since we often deal with shared projects, short deadlines and urgent requests.

How to express your interest?

You should send your documents in a single pdf in the following order:
1. your CV  2. Complete application form.
Please  send  these  documents  by  the  publication  deadline  to
Annika.NASLUND@ec.europa.eu  indicating  the  selection  reference
DGT/COM/2026/1916 in the subject.

No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

Eligibility
For eligibility, please consult this page with all the information needed.
